# Workspace acceptance fixtures

The Native probes below document earlier acceptance runs. Any new runtime run must target its own independent Codlet test client and synthetic conversations, with verified run/profile/registry/PID/Target and backend/home ownership. Historical Target IDs, real conversation lists and an arbitrary first page cannot select that run. Creating a second window alone does not establish data isolation. These fixtures do not run automatically during build or CI.

Commands below run from the Core root. Install dependencies there with `npm ci --prefix frontend`; the `codex/frontend` wrapper uses that same installation. The old provider terminology describes each research fixture, not a requirement to install production Adapters. Review each probe's source and assumptions before a new run. Current SDK and release scope are in [Core documentation](../../../../docs/README.md).

Build with `node codex/tests/fixtures/workspace-acceptance/build.mjs`. This prepares two explicit local test packages under ignored `codex/.artifacts/workspace-acceptance/`; it does not replace official adapters or install anything automatically.

The provider reuses the production discovery, workspace and metadata projector. It preloads base navigation as the production adapter does, but injects no page or composer action. The consumer acquires a real Core-authenticated ticket, creates owned slots/leases/transcripts/shortcuts, records native commit completion and restores its settings navigation. Its Host uses only Core-owned CDP sessions; no second backend connection is created. The script records quantitative content presence and metadata, not message text or credentials.

Preview both directories using the running Core's `runtime.json.cliScript`. Register the provider with `ui.dom` and `ui.mainWorld`, then the consumer with those plus `host.process` and `cdp.raw`, only within an authorized acceptance run. Keep official adapter IDs, directories, source and grants intact. Read the consumer's `report.json`; inspect an existing run rather than replaying uncertain operations. Remove consumer before provider through scoped CLI, retaining report/source files and without forcing deletion or unrelated cascading.

See [the current evidence and limitations](../../../../docs/history/adapters/spec/workspace-review.md). This fixture targets a real Windows client; it is not a normal CI test or a macOS acceptance claim.

## Read-only discovery regression probe

After `node frontend/build.mjs`, run `node codex/tests/fixtures/workspace-acceptance/build-discovery-probe.mjs`. Preview the generated `codex/.artifacts/workspace-discovery-probe` directory through the scoped CLI, then register its temporary `dev.workspace.discovery-probe` ID with `host.process` and `cdp.raw` for an authorized diagnostic run. Read `report.json` and remove that ID through the scoped CLI when done.

This probe evaluates only the rebuilt adapter's definitions and its read-only connection/navigation discovery in Core-owned page sessions. It calls neither `activate` nor `createAdapter`: it does not replace installed APIs, patch transports, mount panes, change routes, reload an adapter or open a backend connection. It counts the old whole-tree boundary up to 20,001 fibers without reading message props, measures the bounded native-shell ancestry and 1,000 connection checks, and preserves errors per target. A current tree below the old limit does not reproduce the original long-session failure; the 72,008-fiber, three-pane regression fixture covers that case deterministically.

## Distinct cold transcripts

Build with `node codex/tests/fixtures/workspace-acceptance/build-cold-probe.mjs` and preview/register the generated temporary `dev.workspace.cold-probe` package through the scoped CLI. Its permissions are `ui.dom`, `ui.mainWorld`, `host.process`, `cdp.raw`. It selects six different cached tasks that are unselected, `needs_resume` and have no stream role: two use the original implementation from commit `bb727175`, four use the current implementation. It mounts owned offscreen containers, records readiness/body lengths/history methods and before/after stream state, and disposes all roots. It sends no messages, changes no route and replaces no installed adapter API. Retain `report.json`, then remove the temporary ID.

## Native navigation receipts

Build with `node codex/tests/fixtures/workspace-acceptance/build-navigation-probe.mjs`. Preview/register `dev.workspace.navigation-probe-provider` with `ui.dom`/`ui.mainWorld`, then `dev.workspace.navigation-probe-consumer` with `ui.mainWorld`/`host.process`/`cdp.raw`. The consumer invokes a temporary capability through Core RPC; the provider uses the exact internal `createThreadOpener` used by Desktop, the existing local manager and the actual native router. It installs no transport interceptor and leaves official adapter symbols untouched.

Run the read-only alternate probe first to preserve tree evidence. Navigation acceptance requires a local selected route and two other already-resumed owner tasks. It measures receipt latency and metadata reads, then restores the original selected route. If those prerequisites are absent it records read-only control RPC timing and performs no navigation. Results are in the consumer's `report.json`; retain completed navigation reports before a control-only run. Remove the consumer, then provider through the scoped CLI. The two modes measure RPC receipt completion, not Native paint completion or a universal latency bound.

## Offline Adapter wrapper matrix

Run `node codex/tests/fixtures/workspace-acceptance/bench-wrapper.mjs`. It bundles the Adapter into a React/jsdom fixture, uses only synthetic thread identities, and writes `codex/.artifacts/workspace-wrapper-benchmark/report.json`. No client, Core registration or backend is used. The report records its source bundle hash, runId, Node version and explicit `nativeClientTested:false` / `nativeDraftHandoffTested:false` fields.

Cases cover 0/1/2/4/5/8 transcript roots, 200 streaming mutations, five bursts of 40 shell mutations, ResizeObserver subscription churn and complete teardown. A separate fake composer driver samples warm binding/state transitions. Its timing is only protocol overhead, not Native editor readiness or paint latency. A settled microtask count is not a sustained idle CPU measurement. See [the agreed Native contract and remaining acceptance work](../../../../docs/history/adapters/spec/workspace-composer-contract.md).

## Owned current Native discovery and baseline

For a new Adapter-only run, `prepare-native-run.mjs <Core-source-directory> <reviewed-lab-binary> <reviewed-sha256>` writes a plan. `prepare-native-profile.mjs <preflight.json> <same-reviewed-lab-binary>` prepares a fresh profile with a real stdin pipe and exits normally before Desktop/backend launch. It never resumes an interrupted preparation or copies credentials/sessions. Use the audited Core isolated-client build/start templates for that same profile, then normal first authentication/initialization when needed.

Run `verify-native-run.mjs <owned-run-directory>` after initialization/restart. This reads actual ownership, dynamic Target, backend effective isolation, authentication/readiness and empty active/archived lists, without writing Native state. `build-native-discovery.mjs <same-directory> [discovery-label]` then creates a new read-only Host probe with the production role discovery and Native scope inspector. It requires that explicit ready/empty evidence again at runtime; Core-owned CDP attaches only its verified Target. Preview/register only the generated temporary ID in that run with `host.process` and `cdp.raw`; read its report and remove the temporary ID afterward, keeping files.

If the generated runtime CLI wrapper rejects the namespaced root, use that client's audited `client/Test-Plugins.ps1` entry point, with `list`, `preview`, `add`, etc. as its arguments (without an extra `plugin` prefix). Verify the returned registry scope against the run evidence. Do not fall back to another Core or edit the registry.

`measure-native-baseline.mjs <same-directory>` records five six-second intervals for the explicit owned roots and all descendant processes, validates creation times/images and rejects coordinator restarts. It never writes input or messages, mounts roots, or uses Computer Use. Any child-process churn invalidates the steady baseline. It includes Core and Native background services; the empty-home sample cannot prove Native pane increments, input/paint latency or draft handoff. Outputs are new files under the owned run, not CI/release acceptance. See [current environment and source evidence](../../../../docs/history/adapters/spec/workspace-native-environment-2026-10-11.md).

## Fixed long history and controlled notification replay

`generate-history.mjs` writes deterministic 20/200/2000-item mixed histories and 1/4-thread notification schedules with a hash manifest to a fresh ignored artifact directory. `replay-desktop-history.mjs` exercises production Desktop Adapter paging, event projection/subscription and teardown with a synthetic manager in a Node VM. Add `--realtime` for successive 60-second schedules at 20 deltas/second/thread and 64 characters/delta. It never creates a Native client, DOM or backend connection, and its report keeps Native history/streaming/paint evidence false.

`inspect-history-protocol.mjs <absolute-codex-executable>` exports only exact public/experimental schemas. `probe-native-history.mjs <owned-run-directory> <protocol-export-directory> --probe` is a separate opt-in capability gate for the execution owner of a running verified profile: create one new disposable synthetic thread, inject two model-context markers once, read canonical history, then clean only that new thread. It sends no model turn and does not modify the protected eight-thread fixture or drafts. Injection acknowledgement alone is not Native history/streaming evidence. See [execution prerequisites, lifecycle and missing capabilities](../../../../docs/history/adapters/spec/workspace-history-acceptance-2026-10-13.md).

## Read-only navigation wait analysis

`analyze-native-selection-profile.mjs <absolute-acceptance-summary.json>` reads an already captured complete Native consumer profile and matches selection/input phases by time and synthetic alias. It writes only phase durations and source hashes, starts no client and does not isolate a matrix window without explicit timestamps. `analyze-navigation-waits.mjs` exercises the production navigation scheduler with injected synthetic bindings in jsdom: synchronous-ready, 130ms-ready with immediate notification, and deliberately delayed notification. It measures neither Native input discovery nor paint. See [actual phase evidence, offline separation and optimization priorities](../../../../docs/history/adapters/spec/workspace-navigation-waits-2026-10-13.md).

The scheduler fixture now records the private opt-in navigation phase points. `summarize-navigation-test-points.mjs <absolute-private-report.json>` reads them offline, avoids double-counting nested checks, keeps missing timed stages null and rejects reconstructed completeness after ring overwrites. See [phase spans, lifecycle and evidence limits](../../../../docs/history/adapters/spec/workspace-navigation-phase-points-2026-10-13.md).

The older profile, shadow, composer and draft-recovery drivers require explicit synthetic `threadIds` for the current owned run. Supply them in the generated package's `targets.json` (`{"threadIds":["…","…"]}`), or `mode.json` for the navigation profile. Historical task and Target IDs do not select a new run. Rebuild Native discovery/navigation/investigation packages after changing their source: the Host verifies the complete `probe.js` hash before evaluation. Existing captured bundles and reports retain their historical scope.
